explanation: The notes describe adolescence as a period of neuronal overgrowth and pruning, with the prefrontal cortex maturing last. This helps explain why reward orientation and emotional arousal can outpace regulatory control, especially during the years when risk-taking is prominent.

options.text: Adolescents generally cannot think abstractly until adulthood
Reward-oriented and emotionally arousing systems intensify before the prefrontal cortex fully matures
Risk-taking in adolescence usually means severe intellectual disability
The adolescent brain is structurally stable after childhood
Risk-taking is mainly caused by a lack of school discipline

rationale: Adolescence involves major brain remodelling.; The prefrontal cortex matures later than systems linked to reward and arousal.; Risk-taking can persist even when an adolescent can describe possible consequences.
